dial.summary: FOMC held at 3.5–3.75% for the fifth consecutive meeting (9–3 vote, with Hammack, Logan, and Kashkari dissenting for a hike), triggering a DXY decline to 100.59 as June PCE came in soft and Q2 2026 GDP advance was released today; BTC Accumulation thesis intact: BTC.D firm at 56.3%, TOTAL stable at ~$2.28T with BTC at $63,888, perp funding near-zero (+0.004%/8h), and DXY falling toward the critical 100 threshold—real yields (2.44%) remain the primary remaining headwind as the long end reprices the hawkish dissent premium.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) June 2026 data remains the latest confirmed read at $102.7T; July 2026 data not yet published across all four central banks; component trajectory: US M2 all-time high $22.7T (February 2026), China M2 YoY ~9%, EU M2 ~$19.4T (March 2026); 4-week trend up (June > May, YoY expansion intact across components); status supportive (4-week uptrend met; YoY contracting headwind condition not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: June 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI confirmed at 53.3% (released July 1)—sixth consecutive expansion month, down 0.7pp from May's 54.0%; July 2026 ISM print releases August 3 at 10:00 AM ET; S&P Global US Manufacturing flash PMI for July edged down to 53.8 from 53.9, offering a cautious advance signal; June sub-indicators: new orders 56.0%, prices paid 73.0%, employment 49.7%; 4-week trend down (54.0% → 53.3%); status neutral (above 50 but falling—supportive requires above 50 AND rising).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot fell to 100.59 on July 30, 2026 following FOMC hold (9-3 vote, July 29) and soft June PCE data released at 8:30 AM ET today; prior close 101.2952 on July 29 (pre-FOMC range 101.011–101.60 over the week); 30-day change: June 30 close ~101.34 vs July 30 100.59 = −0.74%, exceeding the 0.5% relative flat threshold; FRED DTWEXBGS broad index unavailable this run (API blocked)—trend derived from ICE DXY spot; status headwind (above the 100 ICE DXY threshold; approaching neutral zone; supportive requires below 97.5).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant-maturity real yield) at 2.44% as of July 27, 2026 (consistent with the July 23 TIPS reopening auction clearing at 2.438%); post-FOMC July 29 move: 10Y nominal rose 7bps to 4.677% while 2Y fell 4bps to 4.236%, and 30Y hit its highest since July 2007 at 5.244%—suggesting real yield pressure persisted on the hawkish dissent (3 FOMC voters wanted to hike); 4-week trend up: DFII10 rose from ~2.18% on June 25 to 2.44% on July 27 (+26bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold); status headwind (above 2% and rising; soft PCE/GDP today is the primary near-term real-yield compression catalyst).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: Post-FOMC July 29, 2026 (H.15 closing): 10-year Treasury 4.677% (+7bps), 2-year 4.236% (−4bps); spread: 4.677% − 4.236% = +0.441% ≈ +0.43%; the FOMC hold (36% hike risk unwound in 2Y) + hawkish dissenters (term premium in 10Y/30Y) drove the bull-flattener to steepener rotation; 4-week trend flat: spread moved from ~+0.40% (June 30) to +0.43% = +3bps, below the 5bps flat threshold; status neutral (positive spread, 4-week change below steepening threshold; not deeply inverted).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL at $6.75T for week ending July 22, 2026, up $4B from the prior week and $89B higher than a year ago (H.4.1 released July 23, 2026); July 30 H.4.1 release (covering week ending July 29) due at 4:30 PM ET today; 4-week trend flat: balance sheet moved from ~$6.72T (week ending June 25) to $6.75T (+$0.03T = +0.45%), within the <0.5% relative flat threshold; status supportive (flat to marginally growing; QT effectively paused; no aggressive runoff with rising overnight rates).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass returned HTTP 403 again this run; value carried forward at +0.004%/8h (annualized ~+4.4%)—well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; BTC price at $63,888 on July 30 (Fortune/CoinDesk, 1:13 AM EDT), roughly flat from $63,818 on July 29; FOMC hawkish hold (3 dissenters) did not trigger a significant funding spike, consistent with spot-led market and low leverage; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June); status supportive (near-zero funding far from overheating).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$314.68B total (USDT $186.35B + USDC $74.89B per CoinLaw/coinlaw.io June 21, 2026—$314.68B across 382 stablecoins); TOTAL crypto market $2.28T (BTC $1.28T at ~56.3% dominance per TradingView Hub July 2026; BTC.D also quoted at 56.66% per CoinGecko); dominance: $314.68B / $2.28T = 13.8%; 30-day trend down: TOTAL grew from ~$2.1T (June 30) to ~$2.28T (+8.6%) while stablecoin MC held at ~$314B, compressing dominance from ~15.0% to 13.8%—capital rotating from stablecoins into risk assets; status supportive (falling 30-day basis; TOTAL rising while stablecoins held flat).

upcoming.title: BOJ Rate Decision / Employment Cost Index Q2 / UMich Final Sentiment (July 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan monetary policy statement released overnight ET (concluding July 30–31 BOJ meeting)—Policy Rate currently 1.0% following the June 16, 2026 25bps hike; markets expect a hold at 1.0% with Governor Ueda's press conference watched for October/December hike timing signals amid Iran-driven inflation and weak yen dynamics; Employment Cost Index Q2 2026 at 8:30 AM ET (BLS)—Fed's preferred quarterly labor cost gauge, key input for September 15–16 SEP FOMC deliberations; University of Michigan Final Consumer Sentiment (July 2026) at 10:00 AM ET—final 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations will be parsed given the hawkish FOMC dissent on July 29.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Manufacturing PMI for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—first Q3 manufacturing activity read and first significant macro print after the July 29 FOMC 9-3 hold; prior June reading: 53.3% (sixth consecutive expansion month, down 0.7pp from May's 54.0%); S&P Global US Manufacturing flash PMI for July edged down to 53.8 from 53.9, offering a cautious advance signal; markets will watch whether new orders (June: 56.0%) hold momentum and whether prices paid (June: 73.0%) continues its disinflationary path; a print above 54 with declining prices paid would support the BTC Accumulation / soft-landing thesis.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (June 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) for June 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—job openings are a key Fed metric for labor-demand tightness; arriving one day after the August 3 ISM Manufacturing print, this data will shape September 15–16 SEP FOMC expectations on whether the labor market is softening in line with the soft-landing thesis; the hawkish July 29 dissent (3 votes for a hike) makes any sign of labor-market softening more market-moving than usual.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Services PMI for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—companion to the August 3 Manufacturing print; prior June 2026 reading: 54.0% (24th consecutive expansion month, down 0.5pp from May's 54.5%), employment 51.2%, prices index 67.7%; July reading is the second Q3 services data point and will frame September 15–16 SEP FOMC rate expectations alongside the August 7 NFP; a reading above 54 with continued prices moderation would reinforce the case for a September pause and weigh on DXY.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 2, 2026)
upcoming.note: Weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET—the weekly labor market pulse released one day ahead of the July NFP print on August 7; a print near or above 260k would reinforce soft labor market signals and add to the case for a September rate cut discussion at the September 15–16 SEP FOMC; the hawkish 9-3 FOMC split on July 29 means claims data carries elevated market impact through August.
